{{Recipe summary
| Category = Seafood recipes
| Yield = 3 pints
| Time = Prep: 1 day, 1 hour</br>
Cooking: 5 minutes
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{recipe}}

==Ingredients==
*¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*5 cups water, divided
*1 [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] (about ½ [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]]) [[Cookbook:Herring|herring]] fillets
*2 cups distilled or white wine [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]]
*¼ cup [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard seed]]
*2 teaspoons whole [[Cookbook:Allspice|allspice]]
*2 teaspoons black [[Cookbook:Pepper|peppercorns]]
*3 [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaves]]
*3 [[Cookbook:Clove|cloves]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]] (thinly [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]], with rind removed; only the flesh should be left)
*1 medium [[Cookbook:Onion|red onion]], thinly sliced

==Procedure==
#Heat 4 cups of water enough to dissolve salt. Let cool to room temperature. 
#Submerge the herring fillets in the brine and refrigerate overnight, or up to 24 hours.
#Meanwhile, bring the sugar, vinegar, the remaining cup of water and all the spices to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]. [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] 5 minutes, then turn off the heat and let this [[Cookbook:Steeping|steep]] until cool.
#When the herring have brined, layer them in a glass jar with the sliced lemon and red onion. Divide the spices between your containers if you are using more than one. 
#Pour over the cooled pickling liquid and seal the jars. Wait at least a day before eating. Store in the fridge for up to 1 month.

steps.text: Heat 4 cups of water enough to dissolve salt. Let cool to room temperature.
Submerge the herring fillets in the brine and refrigerate overnight, or up to 24 hours.
Meanwhile, bring the sugar, vinegar, the remaining cup of water and all the spices to a boil. Simmer 5 minutes, then turn off the heat and let this steep until cool.
When the herring have brined, layer them in a glass jar with the sliced lemon and red onion. Divide the spices between your containers if you are using more than one.
Pour over the cooled pickling liquid and seal the jars. Wait at least a day before eating. Store in the fridge for up to 1 month.
